meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

examples.text: Добрый день, позвольте нарушить вашу тихую беседу.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, allow me to interrupt your quiet conversation.

examples.text: Разрешите мне прервать вашу милую беседу!
examples.trans: Allow me to interrupt your lovely chat!
A big city.
The sum is very large.

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.
Say hi to the bums.
Not bums — homeless people.

examples.text: У нас есть бомж? Который во дворе живёт?
examples.trans: We have a homeless guy? The one who lives in the yard?

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: I have a toy car.
Childhood was hard.
You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.trans: It's an important question.
I have important business.

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

выгонять.gloss: to drive out, kick out, fire

meanings.en: to drive out, kick out, dismiss, fire
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'гонять').

examples.trans: The chef fires the bartender from work.

examples.text: Шеф, неужели вы выгоняете меня с работы?
examples.trans: Chef, are you really driving me out of work?

examples.text: Я не должен был вас выгонять.
examples.trans: I should not have kicked you out.

meanings.note: Много дел = a lot to do. Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.
Common neuter noun meaning 'matter; thing to do' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I have a lot to do.
How are things?

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: Good afternoon!
I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: About people.
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.trans: Good evening!
She is very kind.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

meanings.note: in threats: ты ещё увидишь = you'll see
Ещё больше = even more.

examples.trans: You've still got some.
You'll be sorry!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.
This is my wife.
I'm with my wife this evening.

examples.text: Но вечером я обещал быть с женой.
examples.trans: But I promised to be with my wife this evening.
I always forget my keys.

examples.text: Дима, не забывай, что ресторан ты мне продал.
examples.trans: Dima, don't forget that you sold me the restaurant.
Come on. Let's forget it!
We'll arrange something for tomorrow.
See you tomorrow!

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

заплакать.gloss: to start crying, to burst into tears

meanings.en: to start crying, to burst into tears
meanings.note: Inceptive за- + плакать.

examples.text: Дима, что это с тобой? Ты чуть не заплакал?
examples.trans: Dima, what's wrong with you? Did you almost cry?

examples.text: Настя, если заплачешь, я тебя оштрафую!
examples.trans: Nastya, if you cry, I'll fine you!

examples.text: Не надо. Если не выпью, я заплачу от горя.
examples.trans: No need. If I don't drink, I'll cry from grief.

examples.text: Кто-то в зоопарке опекает зверя, а мы бомжа опекаем.
examples.trans: Some people sponsor an animal at the zoo, and we look after a homeless man.

examples.text: Женщина, не буди во мне зверя!
examples.trans: Woman, don't wake the beast in me!

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm here.
We live here.
But we're in business here.
What is this, did I walk into a zoo?
Once I went to the zoo.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: person or organization that invests money

examples.text: Вы познакомитесь со всеми нашими инвесторами.
examples.trans: You will get acquainted with all our investors.

examples.text: Крупный инвестор из Москвы приехал на встречу.
examples.trans: A major investor from Moscow arrived for the meeting.

meanings.note: In questions.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: From Latin 'contractus' (agreement, drawing together, from 'contrahere').

examples.trans: My military contract ended.

examples.text: Мой военный контракт закончился, теперь я гражданин.
examples.trans: My military contract ended, now I am a civilian.

examples.text: О, грибы! Мне один дурак на корпоративе дал.
examples.trans: Oh, mushrooms! Some idiot gave them to me at an office party.

examples.text: Но скоро у нас важный корпоратив банка!
examples.trans: But soon we have an important corporate event for a bank!

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Who's there?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: К лицу = suits (someone).
Formal.

examples.trans: It really suits you!
He has a very kind face.

examples.text: Карамельно-сливочный цвет. Очень тебе к лицу! Надень куртку.
examples.trans: A caramel-cream colour. It really suits you! Put the jacket on.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
Our toilet is dirty.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: of things, places, films: 'как называется ...?' = what is ... called?

examples.trans: What's this town called?
The operation is called Golden Yard.

examples.text: Товарищ генерал, операция называется Золотой ярд.
examples.trans: Comrade General, the operation is called Golden Yard.

нарушить.gloss: to break, to violate; to disturb

meanings.en: to break, to violate (a rule, a promise)
to disturb, to interrupt (silence, a conversation)

examples.text: Добрый день, позвольте нарушить вашу тихую беседу.
examples.trans: Good afternoon, allow me to interrupt your quiet conversation.

examples.text: Неужели так сложно один раз нарушить свои принципы?
examples.trans: Is it really that hard to break your principles just once?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: + prepositional; об before a vowel: об этом

examples.trans: I'm thinking about it.
We're talking about the town.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

meanings.note: Core Russian pron meaning 'they' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: They are building a centre.
History will punish them.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

опекать.gloss: to look after, to take care of; to sponsor

meanings.en: to look after, to take care of
meanings.note: Also to sponsor an animal at a zoo.

examples.text: Кто-то в зоопарке опекает зверя, а мы бомжа опекаем.
examples.trans: Someone sponsors an animal in the zoo, and we look after a homeless man.

examples.text: И теперь только я решаю, кого мы опекаем.
examples.trans: And now only I decide whom we look after.

meanings.note: In 'по поводу' + genitive.
+ dative.
'по телефону'.

examples.trans: I'm here about the job.
We're talking on the phone.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Позвольте = allow me (polite).

examples.trans: Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.
Allow me to help you.

examples.text: Прошу, присаживайтесь. Позвольте, я сделаю удобнее.
examples.trans: Please, have a seat. Allow me, I'll make it more comfortable.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

examples.text: Жена твоя большая поклонница, посидишь с ними, пошутишь.
examples.trans: Your wife is a big fan; you'll sit with them, crack a few jokes.

examples.text: Моя будущая жена ваша большая поклонница.
examples.trans: My future wife is a big fan of yours.

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I understand.
I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

посидеть.gloss: to sit for a while; to stay (with someone)

meanings.note: Perfective of limited duration. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть').
Посиди с ним = stay with him. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'сидеть').

examples.trans: Stay with Vika for a while.
Let's sit in a café for a bit.

examples.text: Слушай, я уеду на полтора часа. Ты с Викой посиди, понял?
examples.trans: Listen, I'm going out for an hour and a half. You stay with Vika, got it?

пошутить.gloss: to joke, to make a joke

meanings.note: Я пошутил(а) = I was only joking. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'шутить').

examples.text: Я смотрю, вы легковерный! Я же пошутила!
examples.trans: I see you're gullible! I was only joking!
Don't be offended, I was only joking.

examples.text: Может быть, шеф просто неудачно пошутил?
examples.trans: Maybe the chef just made a bad joke?

meanings.note: + dative of the buyer: 'продать соседке' = to sell to the neighbour

examples.trans: I'll sell it to the neighbour.
He sold the car.

examples.text: Ну, как знаешь. Продам его Клавдии Викторовне.
examples.trans: Well, suit yourself. I'll sell it to Klavdia Viktorovna.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

examples.text: Он слишком молод для ресторанного критика.
examples.trans: He is too young for a restaurant critic.

examples.text: К нам сегодня приедет ресторанный критик.
examples.trans: A restaurant critic will come to us today.
A presumed restaurant critic has been spotted!

meanings.en: to decide, to make up one's mind
meanings.note: Решать, что делать.

examples.trans: Decide for yourselves what to do.
We decide all matters together.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!
examples.trans: Here it is, the phone! Decide for yourselves what to do. Without me!

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?
Polite request. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'казать').

examples.trans: What did you say?
Excuse me, where's the metro?
Tell us, when will your programme be out?
There exist five stages.
There are five stages of accepting the inevitable.

examples.text: Мы очень часто существуем в иллюзиях.
examples.trans: We very often exist in illusions.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I

examples.trans: What is this?
He's so kind.
Pavel Yuryevich, what is this?

meanings.note: To someone you call ты. Core Russian det meaning 'your (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.note: As opposed to before.

examples.trans: Now I'm the boss.
Now everything's fine.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

meanings.note: Not loud.
A quiet spot or street.

examples.trans: Stick it in a quiet spot.
It's a quiet evening today.

examples.text: Лепите на уровне головы, в тихое место.
examples.trans: Stick it at head height, in a quiet spot.

meanings.note: softens a request: только не сердись = just don't be angry

examples.trans: I was only looking.
Just one.
I was only looking!

meanings.en: to trade, to sell, to deal in
meanings.note: + instrumental: торговать овощами = to sell vegetables.

meanings.en: лицом торговать = to be the face (of something)
meanings.note: Colloquial idiom: to show off one's face, look good for business.

examples.text: А твоё дело по контракту — здесь лицом торговать.
examples.trans: Your job under the contract is to be the face of this place.

examples.text: Вы оба мной торгуете, ненавижу вас!
examples.trans: You're both trading me like goods, I hate you!
He sells vegetables at the market.

examples.text: Понимаешь, в Москве существуют такие добрые традиции.
examples.trans: You see, Moscow has such nice traditions.
Our family has a tradition.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: уже четыре года = for four years now

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.en: to have dinner, to have supper

examples.trans: The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Знаменитый олигарх будет сегодня вечером ужинать у нас?
examples.trans: Will the famous oligarch be dining at our place tonight?

examples.text: После смены мы иногда остаёмся вместе тихо ужинать в зале.
examples.trans: After the shift we sometimes stay to quietly have dinner together in the hall.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Чуть-чуть = a tiny bit.
чуть не + verb: я чуть не упал = I nearly fell

examples.trans: I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
